account:
It is day 1, just after eight, and I am in the town hall office for my morning appointment. I read the appointment book and grain inspection brief this morning. The secretary says her morning chest check found only the same three books and no new correspondence. I returned all three books; she has since taken them out and is holding a written book, apparently while preparing the appointment update, though I have not yet seen the completed revision.

Today's main business is the ten o'clock mill grain inspection. I am to ask the miller about stock quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns, then record observations and follow-up decisions. The brief is preparation, not evidence of a shortage or other problem. Lunch at home is at noon, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea with the dockside neighbour at fifteen hundred, and office again at sixteen-thirty.

The additional appointment is an eighteen hundred inspection of the great hall lighting. Builder came to my home last evening and requested that I inspect the completed work in person; I agreed and asked the secretary to add it. I have not inspected the lighting yet.

The only unusual report I know of is the neighbour's vague rumour yesterday about a bridge or port change. The neighbour could not confirm it, and the secretary has received no actual proposal or correspondence substantiating it. I do not know whether any such change is being planned, who would be behind it, or what it would be for. Nothing I have personally seen establishes a connection between that rumour, the grain inspection, and the lighting work.
